name: FL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deeply Republican district with an R+18 partisan lean
Patronis holds a massive financial advantage ($3.8M raised vs $174K)
Prediction markets price the Democrat at roughly 4%
No public polling available to challenge the fundamentals
model.rationale: The R+18 district, Patronis's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising edge, and markets pricing his win at about 95% all point to a Safe R hold; Valimont's modest fundraising and lack of outside opposition spending give no basis to move off that picture.
model.watch: A surprise influx of Democratic outside spending or a scandal involving Patronis would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Florida's 1st District is one of the most Republican seats in the state, with an R+18 partisan lean, and incumbent Jimmy Patronis is running for a full term after winning the seat. He has raised nearly $3.8 million and holds over $930,000 on hand, with more than $2 million in outside support behind him. Challenger Gay Valimont has raised about $174,000 with minimal outside help, and no independent spending is opposing the incumbent.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets give Patronis roughly a 95% chance of winning. With the fundamentals, money, and market pricing all aligned, the forecast expects Patronis to win comfortably, with only modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
